en: Taal Volcano features a unique geological formation where Vulcan Point island sits inside a crater lake on the larger Volcano Island.
The small island province of Camiguin has seven volcanoes, which is more than the number of its municipalities, earning it the nickname "Island Born of Fire."
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Babuyan Channel.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and the third largest in Southeast Asia, covering a massive surface area of about 90,000 hectares.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching 2,954 meters above sea level and featuring three distinct peaks.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site containing over 600 species of fish and 360 coral species.
The eastern province of Samar frequently faces the strongest typhoons because it is the first major Philippine landmass hit by storms crossing the Pacific Ocean.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao were carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago and would stretch halfway around the globe if laid end to end.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate mounds.
The Philippines officially consists of 7,641 islands, an update from the previously taught 7,107 islands after the national mapping authority conducted a newer, more accurate survey.
The Maria Cristina Falls in Lanao del Norte drops 320 feet and generates massive hydroelectric power, supplying most of the island of Mindanao's electricity needs.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea, experiencing ocean tides deep inside the cave.
